\begin{remark}[Consequences of finite-time extinction]
\label{rem:extinction-remarks}
\uses{thm:classification-fundamental-group-free-product, cor:extinction-equivalence}

The extinction argument applies whenever every prime factor has nontrivial
$\pi_2$ or $\pi_3$, without using the sphere theorem. If the initial manifold
is prime, every time-slice has at most one component not diffeomorphic to
$S^3$, and that component has the initial diffeomorphism type. If the initial
manifold is simply connected, every time-slice is a disjoint union of
$3$-spheres; if its fundamental group is finite, each later component is
simply connected or has the same fundamental group. A disappearing component
admits a non-flat homogeneous metric of nonnegative sectional curvature and
has one of the topological types in Theorem~\ref{Theorem1}. The four equivalent
conditions in Corollary~\ref{corequiv} also characterize closed connected
$3$-manifolds admitting a metric of positive scalar curvature
\cite{SchoenYau2}.
\cite{AG,AG,CaoZhu,Cheeger,ChowKnopf,ChowLuNi,ColdingMinicozzi,ColdingMinicozzi,ColdingMinicozzi,GreeneWu,Gromov,Gromov,Hamilton3MPRC,Hamilton3MPRC,Hamilton3MPRC,Hamilton3MPRC,Hamilton3MPRC,Hamilton3MPRC,Hamilton4MPCO,Hamilton4MPIC,Hamilton4MPIC,HamiltonIFTNM,HamiltonNSRF3M,HamiltonNSRF3M,HamiltonNSRF3M,HamiltonNSRF3M,Hamiltonharnack,Hamiltonlimits,Hamiltonlimits,Hamiltonsurvey,Hamiltonsurvey,Hamiltonsurvey,Hempel,Jost,Kap,KleinerLott,KleinerLott,KleinerLott2,LiYau,Milnorsurvey,MorganTian2,Perelman1,Perelman1,Perelman2,Perelman2,Perelman2,Perelman2,Perelman2,Perelman2,Perelman3,Perelman3,Perelman3,Perelman3,Perelman3,Perelman3,Poincare,SPeters,STW,SY,SY,Scott,Shi1,Shi2,Thurstongeom,yuding}.
\end{remark}
